'''The Pile''' is an 886 GB diverse, open-source dataset of English text created to train [[large language model]]s (LLMs). It was constructed by [[EleutherAI]] in 2020 and publicly released on December 31 of that year.<ref name="release paper">{{cite arXiv|first1=Leo|last1=Gao|first2=Stella|last2=Biderman|first3=Sid|last3=Black|first4=Laurence|last4=Golding|first5=Travis|last5=Hoppe|first6=Charles|last6=Foster|first7=Jason|last7=Phang|first8=Horace|last8=He|first9=Anish|last9=Thite|first10=Noa|last10=Nabeshima|first11=Shawn|last11=Presser|first12=Connor|last12=Leahy|eprint=2101.00027|title=The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling|class=cs.CL|date=31 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="host page">{{cite web|url=https://pile.eleuther.ai/|title=The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling|date=13 February 2020|website=EleutherAI Website|publisher=[[EleutherAI]]|access-date=4 June 2023|archive-date=28 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228023753/https://pile.eleuther.ai/|url-status=live}}</ref> It is composed of 22 sub-datasets, including books, movie transcripts, and scientific papers, among other media.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Barr |first=Kyle |date=2023-08-18 |title=Anti-Piracy Group Takes Massive AI Training Dataset 'Books3′ Offline |url=https://gizmodo.com/anti-piracy-group-takes-ai-training-dataset-books3-off-1850743763 |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Gizmodo |language=en-US}}</ref> The Pile and [[Common Crawl]] had been, as of 2024, the two main training datasets being used to train AI models.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Gilbertson |first=Annie |title=Apple, Nvidia, Anthropic Used Thousands of Swiped YouTube Videos to Train AI |url=https://www.wired.com/story/youtube-training-data-apple-nvidia-anthropic/ |access-date=2026-01-29 |work=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028|date=July 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Anthony |first=Aubra |last2=Sharma |first2=Lakshmee |last3=Noor |first3=Elina |date=2024-04-30 |title=Advancing a More Global Agenda for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence |url=https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2024/04/advancing-a-more-global-agenda-for-trustworthy-artificial-intelligence |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Carnegie Endowment for International Peace |language=en}}</ref>

Copyright disputes centering around use of The Pile escalated in 2023, prompting Eleuther to start removing some datasets. Eleuther partnered with various organizations to release Common Pile v0.1 in 2025 in order to have a large curated training dataset without the copyright issues.<ref name=":5" />

==Training on copyrighted works or derivatives==

The Books3 component of the dataset contains copyrighted material compiled from Bibliotik, a [[Internet piracy|piracy]] website.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Knibbs |first1=Kate |date=September 4, 2023 |title=The Battle Over Books3 Could Change AI Forever |url=https://www.wired.com/story/battle-over-books3/ |access-date=13 October 2023 |website=[[WIRED]]}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Roth |first=Emma |date=2024-08-20 |title=Authors sue Anthropic for training AI using pirated books |url=https://www.theverge.com/2024/8/20/24224450/anthropic-copyright-lawsuit-pirated-books-ai |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=The Verge |language=en-US}}</ref>
In July 2023, the Danish anti-piracy group Rights Alliance took down Books3 through [[DMCA]] notices.<ref name=":2" /> Books3 was removed from the Pile before a class action lawsuit was filed in 2024 by three authors seeking damages as copies of the original dataset were still copied and available on the web.<ref name=":0" /> By 2024, The Pile also was taken down from its original site, though was accessible from other file sharing services.<ref name=":4" />

[[OpenSubtitles]] is another dataset used in the Pile that created controversy over the use of copyrighted works, this time from documentaries, movies, television and online videos.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Deck |first=Andrew |date=January 7, 2025 |title=Thousands of documentaries are fueling AI models built by Apple, Meta, and Nvidia |url=https://www.niemanlab.org/2025/01/thousands-of-documentaries-are-fueling-ai-models-built-by-apple-meta-and-nvidia/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250701150709/https://www.niemanlab.org/2025/01/thousands-of-documentaries-are-fueling-ai-models-built-by-apple-meta-and-nvidia/ |archive-date=2025-07-01 |access-date=2025-12-10 |work=Nieman Lab}}</ref>

Tens of thousands of [[YouTube]] videos had their subtitles scraped directly from YouTube and included in the Pile, which YouTube argued is against its terms of service.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Sato |first=Mia |date=2024-07-16 |title=Apple, Anthropic, and other companies used YouTube videos to train AI |url=https://www.theverge.com/2024/7/16/24199636/apple-anthropic-nvidia-salesforce-youtube-videos-training-data-copyright |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=The Verge |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":4" />

== Common Pile v0.1 ==
In June 2025, EleutherAI, in partnership with the [[Poolside AI|Poolside]], [[Hugging Face]], and the [[Library of Congress|US Library of Congress]] and over two dozen researchers at 14 institutions including the [[University of Toronto]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], [[Carnegie Mellon University|CMU]], the [[Vector Institute (Canada)|Vector Institute]] and the [[Allen Institute for AI]], released Common Pile v0.1, a training dataset that contains only works where the licenses permit their use for training AI models.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Wiggers |first=Kyle |date=2025-06-06 |title=EleutherAI releases massive AI training dataset of licensed and open domain text |url=https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/06/eleutherai-releases-massive-ai-training-dataset-of-licensed-and-open-domain-text/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Eriksson |first=Viktor |date=June 9, 2025 |title=Eleuther AI releases 8TB collection of licensed and open training data |url=https://www.computerworld.com/article/4003647/eleuther-ai-releases-giant-collection-of-licensed-and-open-training-data.html |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=[[Computerworld]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Tiku |first=Nitasha |last2=Jiménez |first2=Andrea |last3=Oremus |first3=Will |date=June 5, 2025 |title=Analysis: AI firms say they can't respect copyright. These researchers tried. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2025/06/05/tech-brief-ai-copyright-report/ |work=Washington Post}}</ref> The intent was to show what is possible if ethically training AI systems while respecting copyright.<ref name=":1" /> They found that the process of gathering the data was time-consuming as it could not be fully automated, with humans verifying and annotating every entry, and that resulting models could achieve results that exceeded their expectations even though they were still not comparable with frontier models.<ref name=":1" /> The creators compared the results generated from Common Pile as similar to [[Llama 2]], a model released two years before the creation of Common Pile.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Schuman |first=Evan |date=July 21, 2025 |title=It might be time for IT to consider AI models that don’t steal |url=https://www.computerworld.com/article/4025938/time-to-consider-ai-models-that-dont-steal.html |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=Computerworld |language=English |type=Contributor}}</ref> The model should provide less legal risk to those who use its output if there are fewer copyright issues with the underlying training data.<ref name=":6" />
